- The render gate never refused a run.. Judge: B is clearly better in all four pairs. None of the calls was close enough to need INDISTINGUISHABLE. The B frames show a mature AAA pipeline: dense, specific dressing (signs, neon, street furniture, landmarks), excellent materials (car paint and chrome reflections, aged asphalt and kerbs), skies with real structure, strong aerial perspective, and deliberate cinematic cameras with a clear focal subject. Two of them, the pink-cloud dusk chase (pair 1) and the backlit biplane vista (pair 4), genuinely impress. The A frames all share one profile. On the positive side they have competent warm low-sun lighting with soft shadows, attractive rain-tree canopies, shophouse and Supertree landmarks that give a clear sense of place, and believable hero-car paint. Against that they reuse placeholder-grade assets in every shot: the white box bus with a purple stripe, smooth green blob shrubs, block buildings with flat decal windows, and Supertrees that read as wireframes. They also show untextured or empty asphalt and plazas filling large parts of the frame, flat gradient skies with no clouds or haze band, few and idle pedestrians, a static default gameplay camera with HUD clutter, and occasional clipping bugs (an NPC hand and a cropped vehicle in the frame corners). In priority order, the A fixes are: replace the placeholder vehicles, shrubs and facades with fully modelled assets; fill sidewalks and junctions with active, varied pedestrians, signals, crosswalk markings and kerbside props; give the asphalt grain, wear and a specular response; and add a cloud-structured sky, horizon haze and backlit atmosphere. None of the A frames wows me.
